jc.t: Return to India after the 281 day dharma yatra
w: Flight from Nairobi.

In the evening assembly Swamishri elaborated upon a talk from 'Swamini Vato' : "In times of yore aspirants went in search of God..." Swamishri explained, "An aspirant is one who desires moksha. To attain moksha is the highest and noblest of life's achievements. From an ordinary person one has to ascend to the height of an aspirant and then to the state of a released soul (mukta). God and His holy Sadhu wish to bless all souls with eternal bliss and divine joy..."
An evening assembly of distinguished national and state level dignitaries honored Swamishri.

The evening assembly had an eminent audience of national and state level professionals and dignitaries. After Swamishri's blessings, Dr. Dilip Naiyar, Head of an ICU at Manipal hospital was a changed person. For several months, the heavy grinding responsibilities of his medical duties, had robbed him of mental peace. Dr. Naiyar was on the brink of a nervous breakdown. He told Dr. Akhileshwaran, a Satsangi friend, that one of these days he would run away. And he did take a break. The day he returned Dr. Akhileshwaran informed him of Swamishri's arrival in Bangalore. Dr. Naiyar came to the evening assembly and after listening to Swamishri's blessings he experienced a new breeze of life. He said he had not understood a single world, but the moment Swamishri began his blessings, he felt his tension melt away. He felt unburdened of his worries. "Now I feel totally at peace. It was a different and new experience."
Swamishri performed puja and arti of Nilkanth Mahadev in Veraval (Sapar).
Blessed an assembly in village Moti Vavdi of Rajkot district.

w: C. K. Pithawala, Chandravadan Pithawala and Mahesh Pithawala had come for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. During the conversation, C. K. Pithawala said to Brahmavihari Swami, "Bapa should take complete rest now. Even at this age he is exerting himself greatly. He should not meet anyone."

When Brahmavihari Swami told Swamishri this, Swamishri said, "This is our nature. We simply cannot stay without meeting people." Saying this, snapping the fingers of his right hand, Swamishri said, "I feel restless to meet the devotees."
This was a rare darshan of Swamishri's compassion and affection for devotees!

A youth came for Swamishri’s darshan and blessings. He harboured a desire to become famous through notorious acts. Swamishri restrained him, “You should not earn a name in that manner. Live a value-based life and in obedience to society’s rules and regulations. Obey the disciplines prescribed by our shastras and preserve satsang in your life. Earn a name by being a good devotee. By being rowdy and rough you may get things done but then you’ll have no peace. Refrain from addictions. Do not create commotion at home. Pledge that you will not make anyone unhappy and miserable.” Swamishri inspired the youth with positive attitude and energy.

Today, to give Mahant Swami Maharaj naturopathy treatment, he was laid down so that his head was towards the edge of the bed. In doing so, Swamishri's feet were towards the wall. On this wall was a murti of Shastriji Maharaj. So Swamishri at once said:
"Cover Shastriji Maharaj's murti."
"Why?" the attendant sadhu asked.
"My feet are pointing towards Shastriji Maharaj."
The attendant sadhu said, "But that is up above, and your feet are down below."
"No. Cover it anyway."
Who in this world but the Satpurush would keep such respect for his guru?
The naturopathy advice was that "for now, Swamishri should not eat sweets, fried food, buttermilk or yoghurt". Hearing this, Mahant Swami Maharaj was pleased, clapped his hands and said, "Very good."
These words, spoken happily as good food was stopped, say so much about Swamishri's detachment!
Shri Yashwantbhai Jethva, a senior IPS officer now playing an important role in the security of Prime Minister Shri Narendrabhai Modi, came to take Mahant Swami Maharaj's blessings.
He said, "Now everyone has to follow whatever we say."
Swamishri said, "You yourself used to sing (in childhood), 'We are children of Swami, kings of the world...'"
How wonderfully Swamishri linked such a small thing from 35 to 40 years ago with the present context!
